tells.1: Every list item opens with a bolded label and every risk uses the same 'Mitigation:' line, which reads like a template.
tells.2: Uniformly polished parallel sentences with consulting phrasing such as 'pulled into renewal terms by default' and 'brand pull'.
tells.3: Markdown ## headers in an internal memo, and every mitigation starts with 'We will…' in the same rhythm.
tells.4: The plain-English headings ('What could go wrong, and what we'd do about it') are almost too smooth, and every bullet still opens with a bolded label.

reason: Version 5 is plainly human: it has rough phrasing, vague mitigations and a casual sign-off, but those same traits make it the weakest memo. Version 4 keeps the substance and specifics of the polished drafts while sounding most like a real person talking to colleagues, so it is the best one to send.
